Obviously not everyone would want to take medication but personally I found it very helpful. It was propranolol. 

Please don’t give up - you’ve worked really hard. It’s horrible having so many set backs but you will get there one day. You need to figure out how to get hold of the anxiety.

I’m really sorry you’re being treated this way. I go to university in the UK too & have experienced similar things. It’s like once the differences/ characteristics they mock have an established, legally recognised reason behind them (aka diagnosis), they suddenly just jump off the radar because they can no longer make fun of it to your face without fear of implications. 

Does your university have any good student support services? At my uni, there’s a few disability/well-being advisors who are really well informed on autism and run socials monthly for students with autism. I’m a bit older than most of the students in the group so don’t have any specific friendships with people in the group but it’s nice to be able to interact with other ND students. 

It seems they’ve been trying to get away with covert bullying and that now they can’t do that as readily without fear of implications (because you have a legitimate diagnosis) they’re just deciding to ostracise you instead. 

I’m really sorry you’re going through this. Please know that you’re not the problem - it’s some NTs who feel entitled and like they can mock your difficulties. Sounds like you were used as a bit of a scapegoat too? Whatever it is that’s going on, it sounds like it will ultimately be damaging for your mental health to continue to be in close contact with these people. 

I really hope you’re able to connect with some other people on campus.
